question.problem:
What is the area of the square shown below?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14195146/assets/53ab7a043ebbe03245fd0f8e1bf6438897a30d91654b6e51194205e4c302c07f.png)
question.worked_solution:
The area of a square with sides of length $a$ is given by 

$$
\mathcal{A} = a^2.
$$

Note that each side of a grid cell measures $3\,\textrm{ft},$ and each side of the shaded square covers $4$ grid cells. So, the length of each side of the shaded square is

$$
a = 3 \times 4 = 12 \, \textrm{ft} .
$$

Therefore, the area of the shaded square is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={a}^{2}={12}^{2}=144\,{ft}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
